correctness.rationale: For strictly positive r,gamma,a,D the two-state nonlocal backward equations decouple into scalar k=sqrt(r/D) and h=sqrt((r+2gamma)/D) resolvent modes. The positive and negative half-lines are matched with active values 0/1 and inactive C1 transmission, yielding an exact unique bounded solution because absorption is a.s. The reset-point self-consistency gives P_minus=(1-k/h+k²exp(-ah)/(h(h+k)))/4. Direct derivatives show strict decrease in r and increase in gamma, and exact boundary substitutions show the noncommuting iterated limits. The embedded checker reconstructs all conditions and independent bridge-crossing tests; simulations are not used as proofs.

value.rationale: The incoming-side probability is an experimentally interpretable splitting observable already considered numerically in Figure 5 of the identical-source model, but not determined by the unmarked passage-time transform. A universal exact formula and strict rate-sign laws replace discrete side counting; the noncommuting fast-switching/fast-resetting limits expose a singular observable even when completion-time statistics resemble an always-on gate. This is a physically motivated missing structural result, not merely another parameter setting of the known mean hitting time.
